reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's The Bharunda Birds (Book II) and its frame (the dove king Gay-Neck telling his snared doves); Ryder's two-sentence tale is expanded to six scenes and every addition is disclosed.
The kept beats are accurate: one belly and two necks, nectar found, half refused, the angry head eats poison, the bird dies.

Self-harm safety: the poison is eaten in thoughtless anger, never as a wish to harm itself or the other head. Fixed before approval: the closing moral no longer reads as harm wished on the other head, and the second head's retort no longer sounds like a threat. The death is one calm sentence.

Age band 12+. The vocabulary note that a similar two-headed ಗಂಡಭೇರುಂಡ is on Karnataka's state emblem is correct and hedged. After review the text explains why only one fruit could be eaten. No em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; seams measured exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; one generation plus one edit of panel 5, with the other five panels verified pixel-identical between raw and edit.
Panel 5's necks now part in a V with both heads in dismay (the first version formed a heart shape that read as affection); no eating, falling or death is drawn, and panel 6 is an empty evening shore.
The bird has exactly two heads, one body and two legs in every panel, drawn as a dignified mythical bird; no people or text.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels, not in the app in dark mode.
